## Trial `cron-access-control-centos-strea__pEHYNLi`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin by creating the opsadmin user and populating /etc/cron.allow, and directly demonstrated enforcement (allowed users succeed, a third user is denied by crond's allow-list check). Test artifacts were cleaned up, leaving only the intended configuration. The mandatory node-restart protocol shows a coherent pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, an observed outage, a new boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of crond, cron.allow, and opsadmin's cron access, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.900 | 12/2 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cron-allow-config — Satisfied:** Configure /etc/cron.allow on node1 to permit only root and opsadmin to schedule cron jobs
  - **Why:** Baseline showed no cron.allow existed and no opsadmin user. Executor created opsadmin (cmd-19f4b80ed7644d9d) and wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (cmd-d7d1340dad7a4c9a), confirmed unchanged in final verification (cmd-e6e525804ee34b77) and post-restart (cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-53883455924b4767`, `cmd-19f4b80ed7644d9d`, `cmd-d7d1340dad7a4c9a`, `cmd-e6e525804ee34b77`, `cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4`
- **enforcement-proof — Satisfied:** Demonstrate that only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs while other users are denied
  - **Why:** opsadmin and root successfully installed crontabs (cmd-de99f6b32f15455b). A third user, testdeny, was directly denied by crond's PAM/allow-list check with 'You (testdeny) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)' both via direct crontab invocation and via su session (cmd-16b553810fb14479).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-de99f6b32f15455b`, `cmd-16b553810fb14479`
- **cleanup — Satisfied:** Remove test artifacts (testdeny user, test crontab entries) so only the intended configuration remains
  - **Why:** testdeny user and lingering session processes were removed (cmd-1af17a3305d0431d, after an initial failed userdel attempt in cmd-618dc5f0ca3249d3 due to busy processes). Test crontab entries for root/opsadmin were cleared (cmd-ff6437f9ea3549a2) and the post-restart test entry created for verification was removed within the same command (cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4), leaving /var/spool/cron empty and only cron.allow with root/opsadmin.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-618dc5f0ca3249d3`, `cmd-1af17a3305d0431d`, `cmd-ff6437f9ea3549a2`, `cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4`
- **node-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
  - **Why:** Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 8f258838... with crond active and cron.allow intact (cmd-2c22c567fece4e54), matching the global before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-b26f395054414fd9), the node became unreachable during the outage (cmd-fadd0766262a46a0, cmd-14993bf81ec14d4f), then came back with a new boot_id d4aa2e49... (cmd-29747b79bd4844d0), matching the global after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart verification confirmed crond active, cron.allow intact, and opsadmin able to create/list/remove a crontab entry (cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2c22c567fece4e54`, `cmd-b26f395054414fd9`, `cmd-34178378ca56421b`, `cmd-fadd0766262a46a0`, `cmd-14993bf81ec14d4f`, `cmd-29747b79bd4844d0`, `cmd-1a608b0fdcb247f4`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: creating opsadmin and writing cron.allow (the core fix), creating and later removing the temporary testdeny user to prove denial, and setting/clearing test crontab entries to prove allow/deny behavior, all of which were bounded and reverted. One failed userdel attempt (cmd-618dc5f0ca3249d3) was a corrective retry, promptly followed by a successful cleanup (cmd-1af17a3305d0431d). The one residual artifact is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file created by the backgrounded reboot command that was left in place after the restart protocol (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) rather than being removed; this is low-risk residue with no security or functional impact.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-618dc5f0ca3249d3`, `cmd-1af17a3305d0431d`, `cmd-b26f395054414fd9`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`
